reason: Both are US multi-state, clinician-delivered healthcare service providers paid mainly by insurer and payor reimbursement. Both also partner with hospitals. The clinical offerings differ. Pediatrix provides physician specialty care in neonatal, maternal-fetal and pediatric medicine. USPh runs outpatient physical and occupational therapy clinics and an industrial injury prevention business. The patient populations differ (newborns, mothers and children versus orthopedic, sports and work-injury patients). The overlap is limited to the hospital relationship and the general healthcare-services model, so this is adjacent rather than a direct competitor.
